messages.text: Ali, do you still have Papá's little black notebook? The one with names, bus times, and row numbers written in pencil.
Yes, in the tin with Mamá's coin envelopes. Her Mexico copybook is there too, the pages stop right after long division.
Mamá was sharp with coins. She could make one bag of beans stretch for all of us.
And Papá's pencil notes were neat even when we had to read the notices out loud to him.
Jose at the shop said the fan belt and labor come to about $400 if he does it today.
Tell him yes. I can move it from the credit union account before lunch.
Then we still go to Hanford Friday?
Yes, but we pack sandwiches and I will put the same amount back little by little after the checks come.
Before Teresa comes Saturday, can you leave the blue folder on the table? The one with Oaxaca clippings.
Yes. I put the Mercado 20 de Noviembre page on top, but first I want to add the dentist paper and your knee appointment card.
Ok. We should see what is left after those bills.
Exactly. The pretty pages can wait in the folder until we know.
Mom, sending the school program pictures now. The one with Elena holding the paper came out cute.
I can see her smile clearly on my phone. I printed the last ones and put them by the basket where I keep my thread.
Good. I remember when you made me enlarge everything before you could enjoy the pictures.
Now I just sit by the window and take my time with them. Tell her I noticed the blue ribbon.
Mom, do you want me to grab the Costco detergent and coffee before we come Saturday? I can bring the big pack.
Only coffee this time, mija. The March paper already has $3,278 written before groceries for the weekend.
Ok, coffee only. If you have that yellow folder out, Teresa said she still needs pictures of the two yearly letters.
Yes, I put those with Manuel's clinic papers. There are no extra cards or county letters in that folder.
Sent the school open-house pictures in WhatsApp, Mom. The one with all three kids is my favorite.
I saw them, mija. I am keeping that thread for pictures and little family notes, much easier for me.
Also ignore that long forwarded link Tia's cousin posted under your picture. I'll send you the real flyer from the school page.
Gracias. If I don't know where it came from, I leave it alone.
Are you still coming by the parish hall Thursday? Maria said they need one more pot of something warm.
Yes, I can bring beans with tomatoes. I have enough on the shelf and some green onions outside.
Good. I can bring tortillas if you want.
Bring them only if you see the good price. I am checking the Foods Co paper before I buy anything else.
Are you bringing beans for after Mass coffee Sunday?
Yes, I rinsed the canned ones twice and added garlic, onion, chile, and lime. I will bring warm tortillas too.
Good. I can bring coffee. Maybe one little sweet bread plate for the table?
Just a few pieces cut small, so everyone can have a bite with coffee.
Mami, the clinic portal still shows one consent form under your login and one under Dad's. I can help after dinner.
Mom, I started the tax folder. I see PG&E, property tax, insurance, and the clinic receipts. Still no 1098 or 1098-E, right?
Good. I put both pill boxes by the coffee maker so we do not forget before you call.
Right. Just the county envelope from January and the Smile Dental papers in the blue folder.
Perfect. Also, don't sign the home insurance page until I check it. It lists just you two on the renewal, same as last year.
Ok. Keep the dental receipt with the card statement so I can match the $125 charge.
I will. I like seeing every paper before I send money anywhere.
Okay hija. Manuel is washing the supper plates and I have the papers on the table.
Ma, I sent you the cdc.gov chart and the Fresno County page. The TV station also covered it at 6, same dates.
Mom, the retirement form is asking for past duties. Should I put the years you were on lunch trays first, then the years at the front counter?
I saw the lady on Channel 30. I will print the county page and put it with Manuel's card.
Yes mija. First the kitchen side, then helping with attendance slips and calls when Mrs. Flores needed me.
Good. Ask Dr. Nguyen's office if you want, but the pharmacy has the same schedule posted.
Got it. It also asks for last grade finished. I can leave it as the diploma year from your old file?
Yes, mija. I like to hear it from the office and from the pharmacist before I mark the day.
Use the 1967 one. That is the paper I always gave them.
Teresa called. She said the city form asks for our names from the same house only.
Good. For you, me, Teresa, and Marisol there is nothing to explain. I told her not to put cousins.
Are you still going to that meeting at 6? I can drive if my knee is quiet.
Yes. I want to hear the chief speak, but I also want them to hear about our nephew and those stops near Elm.
The clinic packet is asking the same boxes again. I put the one I usually put and wrote in Mom and Dad's country on the side.
Bring it home. Teresa can look before you mail it.
I also need the old Fresno card from my folder. The one with 9/18/47 on it.
I saw it in the brown envelope by the tax papers.
Mom, Sofia picked teal again for everything. If you still have that soft yarn, she would love something warm for her reading chair.
I have two skeins left. I can make the edges wider so it stays on her shoulders.
She'll wear it all the time. Don't let her try to pay you with her allowance, okay?
No money from my granddaughter. Just tell her to choose a button when you come Saturday.
The kids asked if Saturday is the day with the corn husks again. I told them I would check with you ❤️
Mom, for Mateo's class tree, do you remember if Nana wrote Tepatitlan or the little rancho by San Juan on that old paper?
Mija, she always said the rancho first, then Tepatitlan when papers asked. Papa would say Lagos if he was being fancy.
Yes, but tell them to bring the big foil tray. I put the husks to soak and Manuel moved the extra chairs.
That helps. Did you put both houses on the map when you were sixteen, or just the one outside town?
Okay. I can bring drinks and the little ones can help carry plates, not touch the stove.
Just the one by the vineyard road. Too many names in that house already, your tias and whoever was sleeping in the little room that month.
Good. I will keep the first batch mild so everyone can eat before it gets too loud in the kitchen.
Alicia, are you coming to the 10:30 chair yoga? Linda says she saved the two end chairs.
Yes, I will go. I have Carmen's Fresno recipe note in my purse too, for Beatriz to read after class.
Good. We can sit by the window after. I brought the little prayer card from Sunday.
Gracias, Rosa. I will be there before the music starts.
Coffee after Mass Friday? I can ask Lupe to save us the little inside table, away from the patio door.
Yes please. Last time the outside air kept drifting in and stayed on my sweater all afternoon.
I remember. I will bring my thermos too, no need for the flavored brownie sample they keep passing around.
Gracias. Plain coffee and your pan dulce are plenty for me.
Ma, did the clinic sign-in finally show the March 11 time? Tap visits, not billing.
Yes mija, I found it. I also saw the note they sent after the blood draw.
Good. Tomorrow with Rosa, use the same menu but have her check her own email code first.
I wrote the steps on paper so she can do it at the center.
Mom, I can leave Fresno by 10 Saturday if you still want me to help sort the hallway closet.
Yes mija. I found Daniel's old bat bag and the picture with his blue cap. I put them aside.
Save that one. The little ones will laugh at the knees on those pants.
I also found two tiny handprint cards, so I will keep those in a separate envelope.
Do you still want to stop by St. Paul's after my glucose strips?
Yes. I want the bulletin with the notes about the food pantry vote and the family clinic hours.
Then library box after?
After I read the small print again. I marked most of mine, but I am not signing anything just because a mailer says so.
Mom, Tia Lupe sent me that scary Facebook thing about Measure K. Did you see it?
I saw it, mija, but I am leaving it alone. I want to compare it with the county booklet first.
Good. She asked me to send it to the cousins too.
No, please do not from me. If I cannot find the same thing on the official page, it stays on my phone.
Good morning Alicia. They moved us to the room by the windows today. I saved two chairs near the fan.
Gracias, Rosa. I am doing one small block first while the sidewalk is still cool, then I will come in.
Take the shady side by the church. No hurry, we can start with the easy stretches.
Yes, and no extra loop for me today. My left knee was talking last night.
Mom, the portal shows Quest for Tuesday at 8:30. It says water only after midnight and bring your current bottle list.
Thank you mija. I wrote it on the calendar and put the paper list in my purse.
Also please keep the morning notebook going through Monday. The nurse asked for a full week of numbers.
I have every day except Wednesday. I will do it before coffee so I do not forget.
Mami, do you want me to bring anything from Bakersfield tomorrow? I can stop by CVS too.
Just the small sticky tabs, if you pass them. I used the last ones on Manuel's Wednesday box and the PG&E slip.
Ok. And I found the school photo envelope in my car, I'll bring it with the juice boxes.
Gracias. I wrote Sunday 2:00 on the paper calendar so I won't start beans too late.
Mom, the office was busy today. Three families came in asking about lunch forms and the new bus map.
Ay, send me the map if you can. I want to compare it with what they posted for our district.
I will. Also the PTA room is hosting that listening night Thursday. Mostly parents and two teachers.
Good. I would rather hear them speak first and write my note after.
Ma, I can submit the parish lunch form online tonight. You do not have to write all those names by hand.
Gracias, mija. My fingers were not behaving after chopping onions this morning.
Then leave the sign-up sheet by the phone. Also, please do the beans tomorrow morning, not after Mass when the kitchen is hot.
Yes. Beans early, rice after lunch, trays on Monday. Small pieces.
Mom, I saw the clinic message. It only says to bring the morning numbers and the current pill bottles Tuesday.
Gracias mija. I was going to print it myself, but the password kept spinning. I don't want you doing this after work.
It's okay. Send me a picture of the bottles after dinner and I'll make the list clean.
After I fix his plate and he checks, I will send it. Just one page, not a big project.
I put the folding chairs by the garage door. Do you want the big pot too?
Si, gracias. Rosa wants to practice the verses after coffee, and I promised to show her the old notebook.
The notebook with your pencil marks? I will drive if my knee is not bad.
That one. I still need the page where Mama wrote the chocolate and bread amounts.
Mom, I found that Christmas photo where Tata is holding the red cooler. Want me to send it here or wait until Sunday?
Send it here, mija. I can print it with the ones from your school picnic box.
Sent three. Also, did you still need the way Grandma folded the corn husks? I can ask Tia.
Yes please. Tonight I am writing the little part about December mornings, so that detail helps.
Alicia, I left the empty jar on your porch after Mass coffee.
Gracias. I put a few lemons and the first little red ones in the paper sack for you.
I saw them. So pretty. Your hands must have been busy early.
Only a little while outside before everyone woke up. It made the morning softer.
The new widow sat by herself after Mass. I think your caldo helped her stay a little longer.
I noticed. Next Sunday I will save her the seat near us and bring tortillas wrapped separate so they stay soft.
Good. Also Mateo asked if you can show him how you keep the coffee table moving so smooth.
Yes, I told him I would. I wrote the steps on a card so he does not have to guess.
Did you call Teresa already? You read that clinic paper three times.
Not yet. I made a small list for Dr. Herrera and put it by my purse. I am going to water the tomatoes first.
Good. I can drive after my glucose check if you still want to drop the envelope at church.
Thank you. I will call Teresa after supper, just to make sure I understood the message.
Good morning Alicia, Father left the pantry count on the kitchen table. We have 42 plates for Wednesday.
I will call Elena and Mrs. Cruz after breakfast. If Javi can price the rice and chicken, give him $60 limit and tell him to keep the receipt.
He was nervous last time but he did fine when you gave him the list. I will remind him no fancy extras.
Yes, simple is better. I am keeping this week to Wednesday kitchen and Friday at 6th Street, about eight hours total.
Alicia, are you bringing any clippings for the table after Mass coffee on Wednesday?
Yes, basil and two little geranium starts. I will wrap them after I finish the hem on Manuel's gray pants.
You still do those tiny stitches better than anyone. Your lamp must be working hard.
The lamp helps, but not like before. I do a few rows, then rest and put on the old boleros.
Mom, I checked the county page like you asked. Your name, Dad's, mine, and Mari's came back with no case lines.
Thank you, mija. That matches what I knew, but the form made me nervous.
I also printed the note you wrote about Diego's old car. Keep it short tomorrow, okay?
I will. I am not going to scold everyone. I just want them to teach the young ones better and answer people plainly.
Mija, Father Luis said Sunday they need people for the letter table. Es para las familias nuevas en el valle.
I can sit after 9:30 Mass. I do not like when people talk about those families like one big problem.
Si. Some work harder than anyone and still need help with papers.
We can ask for order and still speak with respect. Bring the clipboard and I will bring pens.
Hermana, did you fill the back of your envelope already? I am taking mine after Mass.
Almost. I am still reading the small print on the hospital board measure and the senior lunch route.
Bueno. I put the prayer list by my purse too. Lupe's grandson is nervous after that meeting at school.
I will call her tonight and just listen. Sometimes people need that before advice.
You left your hat on the kitchen chair. Want me to bring it to the porch?
Please. I am only going to the corner and back before the sun gets high.
Take the cane too if the knee is stiff.
I will. Tomorrow I have the chair class, so today just the flat side of the block.
I'm by the tomatoes. Knee is stiff. Do you still need the wheat tortillas?
Yes, and the plain yogurt. Skip the sweet bread today. Your small box is on the table for noon.
Teresa called me. She says she can bring the pharmacy bag on her way home.
Tell her only if she is already passing. I said yes, but she should not make an extra trip.
Ma, do you still have those little cards you used when parents came in asking about absences? The ones with both ways to say it?
I found a few. Tarde, ausencia, doctor's note, pick-up time. I kept them with the lunch menus.
Perfect. Our new clerk could use examples that sound kind, not stiff.
Tell her simple words help. Many moms were nervous at the window.
Mom, for Nico's family tree, what should I write by Grandpa's old photo with the grape boxes?
Put that he started in the rows and later carried the list for the men riding out before sunrise.
And Grandma? I have the picture of her in the scarf with that metal lunch pail.
She went when the season called, and other days she had keys to nice houses in Fresno. She always counted the grocery money twice.
Alicia, the parish page changed the soup supper to 5:30. I put the flyer picture in our group.
I saw it. I only shared that flyer with Carmen and Teresa, no extra comments.
Good. There is another loud post under it already.
I am leaving that one alone. Also tell me if the page for Elena is really from her daughter before I put anything there.
Coffee after morning Mass? I have my little guide in my purse, the one with the school bond pages.
Yes. I marked two paragraphs I do not understand. We can talk, but I still want to fill mine out quietly after lunch.
Alicia, the little bell on the clinic page has a red number again. Is that where you clicked yesterday?
That is best. Also someone sent me a long message about the bond last night.
Yes, press the bell, then messages. Do not press pay bill.
Bring it if you want. I will read it, but I am not sending those things around.
Gracias. Mine says bring the blue card. Did yours say anything after your test?
Mine had numbers and a short note. Teresa said I can ask them about it Tuesday.
Are you coming to the center at 10, or should I save your chair near the door?
Save the door chair, please. I will skip the floor part and leave before the sun gets strong.
I will carry the books box. You just bring the prayer cards in the small bag.
That helps. The big box and the steps are too much together today.
Are you coming to chair yoga tomorrow or is it another Fresno day?
Fresno again, just for the paperwork visit. I am taking the cooler so we don't buy lunch there.
I can save you a plate from the parish kitchen for after.
Gracias. I am watching the account until the car money is put back.
Mom, before I call, can you put the Blue Shield letter and Manuel's clinic printout by the phone?
They are in the green folder. I clipped the lab time to the March page and put the receipt in the little white envelope.
Perfect. Also keep the confirmation number from the portal page, por favor. We may need it Monday.
I wrote it on the yellow pad next to the phone.
Mom, do you want me to order the paper towels with my app? They have a coupon tonight.
No mijita, save it. I moved the chicken to tomorrow and made lentils with carrots from the garden.
Okay. Are you still making the tray for Marisol's kids Saturday?
Yes. I will use the cans I have and only buy fruit if Save Mart is lower than Foods Co.
Comadre at church said the county office wants every little paper now. Did Teresa finish yours?
Almost. I sent her the bank page with the two deposits and the dentist bill from February.
Ay, the teeth always cost too much. Was that the month you wrote $3,700?
Yes, that one. Usually I try to keep the notebook closer to $3,100 or $3,300, but that bill did not listen.
Ali, acuerdate que en la mesa Papa no dejaba que contestaramos con puro 'yeah yeah'. Decia, habla bien con tu mama.
Ay si. Then the bell rang and all day it was Miss Carter, spelling tests, and keeping my accent quiet.
Y la prima Lupe estaba con nosotros ese semestre, no? She slept by the sewing machine.
Lupe, then Tio Beto for picking season. Mama still made room somehow.
Mija, I found Tia Luz's story about the women selling mole in the plaza. Do you want it for your little notebook?
Si, please. I saved space next to the Oaxaca pictures. I want the names right, not just pretty buildings.
I will tell you after Mass Sunday. How is Manuel's sugar today?
Better after lunch. We are staying close to home until the doctor says his numbers and knee are steady.
I moved the folding chairs from the garage. Do you want six or eight by the window?
Eight, please. Carmen likes room for her purse, and I promised Marisol the children could sit where I can help them with plates.
I saw your list on the counter. Beans first, rice at 4, chicken covered.
Thank you. If the table is ready early, everyone walks in calm and nobody feels like extra work.
Ma, sending the school program pics now. Bakersfield traffic was awful but we made it.
I got them. Tell the big kids I saw their smiles, and kiss the two little ones for me.
They want the old story about Uncle Danny sliding in the dirt after class.
Ay, I still remember washing that uniform before dinner.
Mami, for Tia Lidia's anniversary, should I bring the bubbly bottle or the grape one for you and Dad?
Bring the grape one for us. If they do a toast, I only need the little sip they pour for everyone.
Okay. Also cousin Danny said he is bringing those bakery squares from the new shop near Union Ave.
Tell him I will take the regular pan dulce. I like knowing what is in it.
Mom, the school family-history sheet asks where Grandma and Grandpa came from. Can I put Jalisco for him and Michoacan for her?
Yes, mija. Put that they came here from there, and put that I started out in Fresno.
There is another line with little boxes and none sound right.
Leave a note if they let you. Those boxes were never made with our families in mind.
Mom, I typed the sign-up sheet like you asked. Do you want the headings in English first or Spanish first?
Spanish first for the singing pages, English first for who brings food. Some of the younger ones read one better than the other.
Okay. And stop saying you are not good with papers because you only went through 12th grade. Your notes are more organized than mine.
Ay hija, I just do it slow. Make one line for candles and one line for the small images too.
Do you want me to move the hose before I sit down?
Leave it by the tomato cages, please. I still need to give the chile row a slow drink.
Okay. Teresa called too, I told her you were outside.
Good. I will call her after I pick the few loose lemons for her bag.
Mom, kids are coming by next weekend after the school thing. Do you and Dad need anything from Bakersfield?
We did the pharmacy stop yesterday, so only bring the pictures. My arm is a little sore but I am making soup.
Aww rest it. Teresa said you checked the county paper first, very you.
I keep those things in the folder. When the children visit I want the house calm, no guessing.
Alicia, I saved two seats near the aisle for tomorrow. Easier for Manuel's knee.
Gracias. I will bring two pan dulce from the bakery, one plain for him.
Good. Do you still want just the little bunch of kale from my garden?
Yes, just enough for our soup pot. The big bag goes bad before we finish it.
Ma, I made a folder on your laptop called Family Pages. Inside are Photos, Recipes, Tree Chart, and Dad Stories.
Ma, I found the potholders in my drawer again. The thick ones you made are the only ones that don't burn my fingers.
Gracias. I put the yellow notebook beside the laptop so I can copy a little without losing the papers.
Good. I saved that striped cotton because it washes better. I can do two more before Easter if my hand rests tonight.
I'll bring you the beige thread. And please let me at least buy lunch this time.
Good. Put dates when you know them, even approximate. I can clean the typing later.
Lunch is fine. The little things are for my girls.
I only did one page today, but it made my chest feel less tight after all the clinic mail.
Saliste de misa? Father Ben dijo que puede quedarse unos minutos si quieres hablar.
Si, gracias. I wrote the three things down so I don't talk in circles.
Bueno. Luego me llamas. Put the beans on low and sit outside tantito.
Comadre Lupe asked after Mass if you still toast the chiles before the sauce.
Si, poquito, then I blend it with the spices. Not too much because Manuel says it smells strong.
I will. I already told Rosa I cannot take the extra kitchen shift this week.
Ha. Tell him that smell is why everyone stays near the kitchen.
I saved you some with rice if Teresa can take it when she passes Fresno.
The hardware store has the patio chairs on sale today. Do you want to go look?
Maybe just look. The roof tune-up, county check, and Dr. Nguyen's $85 are all this week.
We can wait on the chairs. The old ones hold for Easter.
Thank you. I sleep better when the regular papers are handled first.
Mom, want me to bring the pan dulce from Bakersfield when we come Saturday?
Bring two, not the whole box. We can cut them for coffee after lunch.
Okay. Kids asked if you are making chicken tacos again.
Yes, with cabbage, avocado, pico, and just enough tortillas for each plate.
Comadre, se me olvido preguntarte el domingo si Rosa llevo los nopales al cafecito.
Si, and Linda took some for Beatriz. We were laughing because I had just seen them at the center on Wednesday too.
Ay, que bueno. Aqui en Fresno sali rapido despues de misa, mucha gente.
This Sunday I will call you earlier, before Manuel wants lunch.
I am at Walgreens. They have two ready for you, one small white bottle and one refill for the night tablet.
Please check they are 90 days, not 30. Last time the clinic changed one and I do not want to mix old with new.
The paper says 90 days on both. Copay is $11 each.
Gracias. Put the receipt in the envelope by the phone and I will update my purse list tonight.
Mom, Diego said he can send you the dates he remembers. Two were by the school exit and one by the gas station.
Tell him only if he is comfortable. I do not need every detail, just enough so they see why I asked about cameras and supervisors.
He said okay. Also he laughed that Tia Alicia is more organized than all of us.
I learned from keeping our own papers clean. Your sister found nothing under this roof, so I want my notes clean too.
Ma, the Fresno County page has the Measure K text and the short fiscal note. I can call after dinner if the small print is hard.
Gracias. I already read the booklet twice, but I want your eyes on that one sentence before I close the envelope.
Okay. Do you want me to tell you how I am marking mine?
No, just help me understand the sentence. I will mark mine after we hang up.
Mom, did you see the Coalinga Senior Center post? Chair yoga moved to Room B on Friday.
Yes, I opened Facebook after dinner for that and your cousin's baby pictures. That is enough for me tonight.
Perfect. And don't answer the man asking people to send him card numbers in the comments. I reported it.
Ay no, I never put numbers there. I closed it and called Carmen instead.
Hermana, Lupe no sabe entrar para ver lo que le mandaron de la oficina del doctor.
Dile que traiga su teléfono después de misa. Yo practiqué con el mío para cambiar la cita de Manuel.
También pregunta de la vacuna de abril, no sabe dónde escoger la hora.
Está bien. Primero miramos el correo para el número, luego las horas disponibles.
Prima Eva quiere que nos sentemos afuera manana. Pero su yerno siempre hace ese humo en la esquina.
Ay no, mejor adentro cerca de la cocina. Me arden los ojos y luego el olor se queda en el pelo.
Si, y despues sacan las charolas raras. Yo le digo que nos guarde fruta y cafe.
Gracias hermana. Fruta, cafe, and maybe one bite of cake for the blessing.
I put the box by your chair. It has your old badge and that picture with the hair net.
Gracias. Check if the envelope with my 1967 paper is in there too.
Yes, and some yellow notes with names and phone numbers. Some are in Spanish.
Found another envelope in the garage. Says Delano 1966 and has your dad's name with numbers beside it.
Those were for calling homes when the children were out.
That was his pay envelope. Keep it with Mamá's little paper where she divided rent, beans, church, and shoes.
There is also a photo of your mom near a long table with crates.
Put that one aside too. She only went for those months, then back to the houses with her apron and key ring.
I put the folding chairs by the garage door.
Thank you. Teresa said Fresno first, then Daniel may come after his Hanford errand, and Marisol is checking the Bakersfield drive.
Do we still have the small plastic cups?
Yes, enough for the older bunch and the two tiny ones. I found them with Daniel's old mitt.
We can bring dessert tomorrow. Please don't make too much, Ma.
I already soaked beans and picked chiles. I will make enough so you take some back.
You sure? I can stop at Costco on the way.
Mom, the school office has that petition again for lunches during spring break. Want me to send you a picture?
Yes, send it. Children should eat even when the adults are fighting over numbers.
Only if strawberries are a good price. I passed on the new fabric today, so the kids can have fruit and juice.
Some parents are saying families should handle it alone.
Families must do their part, but a town has duties too. Same as we check on abuelitos when the heat starts.
Lucia wants to help with tamales Saturday but she gets embarrassed when the masa tears.
Tell her I saved the small spoon for her. We will practice on the broken hojas first, just us at the end of the table.
She will like that. Do you still want me to bring cups and the lemonade?
Yes, and bring the blue sweater for Uncle Ray. He gets cold and never says anything until after dinner.
Mom, the kids asked why you printed the band photo from Oaxaca. They liked the big drum.
Tell them Grandma wants pictures with sound in them, if that makes sense. Plaza, band, ladies cooking, old stories.
It does. Want me to look for hotel prices?
Not yet, hija. First Manuel's April visit, then my glasses, then we count the envelope again.
Hermana, despues de misa Rosa dijo que en la tele cambiaron otra fecha. Ya viste?
Si, lo vi anoche. Teresa tambien mando un articulo, pero voy a llamar a la oficina de Dr. Nguyen el lunes.
Bueno. Yo me confundo con tantos papeles.
Por eso guardo solo el canal, lo que manda Teresa, y la hoja del condado. Lo demas lo borro.
Hermana, found Tia Lucha's paper. It says clavo, canela, and 6 piloncillos for the big olla.
Gracias. Does it have the line we used to sing before the prayer?
Only half. I can send a voice note after Mass tomorrow. Your handwriting is on the back with all the family names.
Send it when you can. I want the children to hear it the old way, not just read the words.
Hermana, did the cold night hurt the little plants?
No, I covered the tomatoes with old sheets. The chiles look stubborn but fine.
Bueno. Save me one if they behave.
I will. I was out there after supper and did not want to come back in yet.
I'm by the closet. Which bag goes to Carmen tomorrow?
The paper one with the lavender square on top. The small pillow cover is under it so it won't wrinkle.
There is also a lady from church asking if you made more for the raffle table.
Tell Rosa I only finished Carmen's and the baby blanket. I can bring cookies for the table.
Alicia, for the parish food boxes they asked if you want a bag put aside too.
Thank you, Rosa, but give mine to Mrs. Luna. We are okay if I keep March close to the $3,200 paper.
I will tell them. Did the office ask you for a card number like last year?
No card number here. Teresa just asked for the two regular letters and Manuel's old folder.
Mom, I opened the portal form. For the background section, do you want me to copy last year's answer?
Yes, use the same main box, and add the note about my parents being from Mexico.
Got it. For place, I wrote Fresno, California, and for date I copied 09/18/1947 from your card.
Thank you. Those forms make simple things so tangled.

Lo hice con tomato, ajo, poquito comino, and caldo from the chicken instead of the cube.
Mándame foto. Después de la comida lo miro con calma; estoy terminando dos páginas de mi libro.
Ah, voy a probar asi. Todavia guardaste pan para el cafecito?
Si, nomas half for me and the rest for Manuel later.
Antes me pedías que te lo leyera por teléfono. Ahora nomás me corriges si sale borrosa la foto.
Jaja, sí. Si no está borrosa, la veo. Luego te llamo y te cuento si Rosa va también.
Comadre Elena dice que cambió ventanas y ahora tiene pagos cada mes. Muy bonito, pero caro.
Ay no, Carmen. Nosotros guardamos para reparar una cosa a la vez. Esta casa ya nos conoce.
Sí, mejor despacio. ¿Ya mandaste lo del dentista?
Mañana mando $85, y después no compro nada extra hasta que cierre la tarjeta.
Alicia, para los tamales de Mama era manteca tibia, no caliente. Y ella ponia el chile en la mesa azul.
Eso queria saber. I wrote the blue table part before I forgot.
Tambien Papa siempre llegaba con polvo en las botas cuando trabajaba por Huron. Eso ponlo si quieres.
I will add it after Mass coffee. These small notes are easier when you remind me.
I have squash and green onions from my yard. Want them for your pot today?
Yes, thank you. I am making a big soup after church and can add them with the carrots.
I will leave them in a bag by the side door before coffee.
Come take a bowl later if the house is not too crowded. I made tortillas this morning.
Mom, I scanned the page with your sophomore attendance. Is 'near Biola turnoff' right for the address note?
Yes, not in town. The bus took forever from there, especially when my brothers missed it.
And for Nana's recipe card, do I keep the front exactly as she wrote it? The teacher note on the back is in a different hand.
Keep both. Front is how she talked to us at home, back was for school.
Comadre, after Mass Rosa said her back pills made her dizzy. Did your knee settle down?
A little. I only used the plain one Dr. Singh allows and ice. I do not touch the strong ones unless he says.
Good. You always keep that list in your bolsa. Take it Friday when you show him the cuff notebook.
Yes, and Teresa printed the lab page too. I clipped it with the Walgreens receipts.
Mom, should we come Saturday morning or later? Kids want to bring the lemonade cups.
Later is better, mija. I do my little walk before breakfast and then stay inside when the yard gets bright.
Ok after 4 then. Want me to bring the folding chair for the patio?
Yes please. After the Tuesday chairs my knee is happier if I sit more than stand.
Alicia, coffee after chair yoga? I saved the handout from last night's library circle.
Yes, thank you. I want the phone numbers for the clinic ride and the people helping with papers for the packinghouse men.
I also wrote down what the young speaker said. We can pray for her family at Thursday group.
Bring it, please. I am going to read it before I answer anyone at home.
Hermana, Rosa said the captain at the senior center was very polite with everyone.

Y lo de Diego? Did you say it?
Only a little. I said a young man should not feel watched just because his car is old and he is driving home.
Linda asked if you are still coming Friday for loteria after lunch. Beatriz has your book in her tote.
Yes. I saw you all Sunday and today, so Friday makes my third outing this week.

I moved the grocery trip to 8:30. Just milk, tortillas, eggs, and your strips today.
Good. I can drive but let us park close.
Yes. I am taking the little cart and no big water case. We can do produce Saturday.
Saturday early then. I will lift the bags.
Do I take the little white one before breakfast or after?
Before. Look at Thursday morning on the chart, top row. I left it beside your coffee cup.
Okay. I can drive after lunch if you still need the bank and post office.
Yes, please. The stamped envelopes are in my purse, and the bank slip is tucked in the small notebook.
Mom, I'll be in Coalinga Saturday. Want me to take Dad to the 10:40 lab so you can finish the soup?
Ay no, you have the kids. I can go with him and put the soup low before we leave.
Kids are fine with Oscar. Text me the paper and I'll park by the side door.
Okay, mija. Only the ride there. I will bring his snack and the little notebook.
Hermana, Rosa dijo que la familia de Lupe necesita comida para el fin de semana.
Tengo arroz, frijol y calabacitas. Puedo hacer una olla y mandar una tarjeta pequeña.
Dios te lo pague. No te canses mucho.
No voy al restaurante con las señoras hoy. Mejor paso por Grocery Outlet si el aceite está menos que en Save Mart.
Hermana, te mande por WhatsApp la foto de la nina con su vestido. Tambien vi el aviso de la misa de San Jose.
Si, gracias. Mande la foto a Marisol y apunte la hora de la misa.
Hermana, encontre la foto vieja de Mama con el vestido azul. Atras dice Fresno, Sept. 1947.
Ay, guardala. That was the month everyone came to see me.
Y lo de Roberto, su hija puso una pagina. Yo la conozco de la iglesia.
Entonces si pondre algo pequeno. Cuando son nombres que no conozco, mejor no.
Tambien encontre el papel de Papa con Mexico escrito fuerte, como el siempre hacia.
Good. Those old papers explain us better than the little boxes do.
Do you need the truck at noon for the 6th Street lunches?
Only if your knee feels okay. I have two trays, the ride cards, and the little notebook for Sofia.
Sofia is the young one who helped with phones?
Yes. Today she makes the first calls, then I check the addresses. This puts me at nine hours for the week, so tomorrow I stay home.
I put your blue folder and the little scissors on the kitchen table.
Thank you. I want to finish that sleeve before the 7 o'clock music starts on the radio.
Do you need the big glass from the drawer?
Leave it there for now. The needle is clear enough by the window, and after that I will water the pots.
Coffee after Mass or are you going straight home today?
Coffee for a little bit. I left soup in the slow cooker and my notebook is in my bag.
Bring it. We can sit by the side door, nice and quiet. I put you on the prayer list like you asked.
Thank you, Rosa. After that I will walk home slow and not sign up for anything else today.
Coffee after Mass Sunday? I have the senior center notice about rides to Fresno clinics.
Yes, save me one. Manuel says the van matters more than half the speeches people mail us.
Also the parish pantry is short rice again.
I will bring a bag. We should help the old ones, the children, and the workers who cannot miss a shift.
Alicia, Maria's grandson needs help filling the lunch form. His abuela understands better if someone explains it slow.
I can sit with them after coffee Sunday. I still remember the words from the front window.
Gracias. Bring that neat folder if you have it, the one Teresa was asking about.
I will bring the old cards, not the big papers.
For the church memory table, should I bring the old tin lunch pail display?
Yes, it reminds me of both of them. Papá with dust on his boots and Mamá with her scarf tied back.
I can add plain paper and pencils for people to write family notes.
Good. Papá trusted pencil lists more than forms, and Mamá always wrote the week's coins on scraps before buying anything.
Mom, I balanced the worksheet. The two deposits together are $4,200, and your March notes are at $3,246 before the pharmacy receipt.
That sounds right. The pharmacy was $18.40, and Manuel's strips were already counted last week.
Good. I left the sections blank where you told me there are no cards, no rent letter, and no separate monthly check.
Gracias. I only know the two regular ones, so blank is correct.
Mom, the portal saved your intake. Nurse only asked me to confirm the three habit lines because they were all 0 again.
Mom, the portal says the Fresno office can put Dad's April visit and the scan on the same morning if you call Monday.
That's right. Put the note about weddings and New Year's, just the little glass for the toast.
Good. Two trips in one month is too much gas and sitting for his knee.
Done. I also wrote that you prefer regular desserts and plain tea when people bring special treats.
Mom, I got your voicemail. Mrs. Alvarez called me too and said you already brought the casserole.
Do you want me to print the estimate page from work?
Good. When I am upset I call you or Carmen, I don't reach for anything from the table.
She needed dinner before her son arrived. I left it with heating notes and put the medicines paper under the magnet so it would not get lost.
Yes please. I already put back the first $75, and after April 3 I can do another piece.

I am sitting with tea. I just wanted to finish what I said I would do, then the house is quiet.
Hermana, the lavender one kept me warm at Mass this morning. Everyone liked the little stitches on the edge.
I'm glad it stayed put. I made it longer because those pews are cold near the side door.
Lupe asked where she could order one. I told her to ask you, pero despacito.
Ay no, I have Teresa's blue pieces next. If Lupe needs warmth, I can show her the pattern after coffee.

Yes please. If they hear the tune, they follow better. I will bring the bread list and the little basket.

I was scared of doing it wrong. Now I just pray, write names, and ask for help.

Please. Teresa said she is bringing the pan dulce, so I need room by the rice and eggs.

Then wash the big pot lid for me before they arrive.
I found the old cake knife in the garage box. The handle is loose.

events.title: 9:00 Mass, then calls and coffee
events.location: St. Paul parish hall, Coalinga, CA
events.notes: After service: llamar a Carmen en Fresno. Coffee table with Rosa, Beatriz, Linda before heading home.

events.title: Morning cuff note + pill tray
events.notes: Write the two cuff numbers in blue notebook before breakfast. Fill Sunday-Saturday tray from current bottles only; keep purse list updated.

events.title: Back patio before breakfast
events.notes: Tie two cages, check chile starts, put small lemon bag by side gate for Rosa.

events.title: Manuel - Dr. Ruiz follow-up
events.notes: Bring blue folder, meter notebook, pill list. Teresa said she can meet us at the desk if the portal paper is confusing.

events.title: Kitchen table: pill box, stamps, wall calendar
events.notes: Check red March envelope before 8:25 phone bell. Put clinic card in Teresa tray.

events.title: Morning errands - short list
events.notes: Go early before it gets warm. Bring rolling cart, jar opener from kitchen drawer, and take bench stop by the pharmacy.

events.title: Senior Center chairs with Rosa
events.location: Coalinga Senior Center, 220 E Forest Ave
events.notes: Bring water bottle. Park on shaded side if spaces are open. Leave mat at home.

events.title: Parish hall: breathing practice + phone basics
events.notes: Bring sign-in sheets, password handout, $35 snack receipt, and the small cash box. Let Javi run the first 15 minutes; Alicia checks the list and keeps time.

events.title: Drop envelopes at county box
events.notes: Bring parish bulletin clipping, senior center flyer, and the sheet Teresa printed about school meals. Check Manuel's envelope before sealing.

events.title: Parish hall: candles, song sheets, kitchen list
events.notes: Bring old binder, Spanish copies, guitar stand count, cinnamon, masa estimate, and names for 9-night route.

events.title: County packet at kitchen table
events.notes: Read the blue guide pages before sealing anything. Ask Teresa about Measure K wording; ask Rosa what parish ladies heard, then decide here at home.

events.title: Blue notebook + old kitchen box
events.notes: After dishes: two calm pages, then label Mama's tamales card and the small stack of Fresno photos.

events.title: Blue notebook + short walk
events.notes: Write 3 lines before errands. Rosary on kitchen table. Walk to lemon tree and back. Cross off two errands, leave the rest for Friday.

events.title: Set hall tables and soup trays before 11:30 lunch
events.notes: Bring labeled serving spoons, extra foil, sign-in sheet, and two small containers for Mrs. Delgado and Mr. Pineda after cleanup.

events.title: City listening night - community room
events.location: Coalinga Community Center, 155 W Durian Ave
events.notes: Bring blue folder. Ask about academy hours, body cameras, and complaint follow-up. Mention older tan Corolla only if there is time.

events.title: Read Coalinga agenda packet
events.notes: Mark pages on school bus stop change, clinic van hours, and water-rate item. Write two questions before Friday forum at parish hall.

events.title: Manuel - Hanford appointment
